solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Manage to hold everything together with current steam organ

indicators.note: to hold means the first word wraps itself around what follows

parts.note: to manage is to cope
everything means all
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone managing a fairground's steam-driven organ while keeping everything running.
explanation.definitionFit: A calliope is the American name for a steam-whistle instrument heard at fairs and on riverboats.

clue.text: Projecting course of ring road in county (northern)

indicators.note: in says the road and ring go inside the county

parts.note: a ring is round, so it gives the letter O

explanation.surface: Plans for a ring road through a northern county.
explanation.walkthrough: A cordon in architecture is a projecting band of stones along a wall; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In building, a cordon is a string course, a horizontal line of stones jutting out from a wall.

clue.text: Restricted American university breaking into song

indicators.note: breaking into means one piece forces its way inside the other

parts.note: a lied is a German art song
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A restricted American college student suddenly bursts into song.
explanation.definitionFit: Limited means confined within bounds, just as restricted does.

clue.text: Theatre manager with prime positioning above dress circle

indicators.note: above puts the first piece over the next in this down entry
positioning means arranging, so these letters are placed in a new order

parts.note: a sari is an Indian dress
a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A theatre boss arranges the best seats above the dress circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress circle' looks like theatre seating, but splits into a dress and a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario organises and finances theatrical productions or concerts.

clue.text: Means soldier in company has more when other ranks are gone

parts.note: a private is a soldier of the lowest rank

indicators.note: when introduces the condition under which letters leave the word
are gone means those letters disappear from the word before it

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks

explanation.surface: A soldier in a unit is better off once the other ranks leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means' is a noun, as in a person of means.
explanation.definitionFit: A private income is money not earned from work, so one's means or wealth.

clue.text: Upturn in iron making plant

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
an upturn is a rise

explanation.surface: A rise in the iron industry leads to a new factory being built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory beside 'iron making', but it is a salad leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Frisee is curly endive, a leafy vegetable grown for salads.

clue.text: Crucifix with diamonds affixed to jumper

indicators.note: affixed to means the letter is attached to the end of the jumper

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo, an animal that jumps
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A cross decorated with jewels pinned onto a woolly sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a sweater (the British word for one) but is a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is a cross or crucifix, especially one set above a church screen.

clue.text: A point in society setting up arts corporation

indicators.note: in a down entry setting up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: corporation is a jocular word for a pot belly, so tum

explanation.surface: Someone notable sets up an arts company.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation as a word for a paunch is old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratum is a level or class within the layered structure of society.

clue.text: Condemn river vehicle that's worn out

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
a crate is slang for an old, dilapidated car

explanation.surface: Someone denounces a battered old car by the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or curse something as detestable.

clue.text: Drink minutes after game

indicators.note: after places the minutes piece behind the game piece

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Players have a drink a few minutes after the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane, a classic alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Repairs the brickwork of the church here? It could be a little light

definitions.text: It could be a little light

parts.note: to point brickwork is to renew the mortar between the bricks
the church here is our church: OUR plus CE, the Church of England

explanation.surface: A builder repointing the local church wonders whether a small lamp would help.
explanation.walkthrough: In physics a point source is a light emitting from a single point, so a tiny light is an example; 'It could be' flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: In optics a point source is an idealised emitter of negligible size, such as a small distant lamp.

clue.text: All are expected to conform with these arresting ideas?

definitions.text: All are expected to conform with these arresting ideas?

parts.words: All are expected to conform with these arresting ideas
parts.note: in Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four a force arrests people for their ideas, enforcing conformity

explanation.surface: Everyone must fall in line with striking new concepts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arresting ideas' reads as striking ideas, but means arresting people for their ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: In Orwell's novel, this secret force detects and punishes unorthodox thinking.

clue.text: Dry goods may be carried here

definitions.meaning: an idiom for abstaining from alcohol
literally, freight is carried ... of a goods train

explanation.surface: A dry goods store's merchandise travels by cart.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone teetotal for a while is said to be on the wagon, and freight rides literally on a wagon.

clue.text: Dismissing editor, looked intently for a brilliant one

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so these letters are removed

parts.note: to look intently is to stare; stared is the past tense

explanation.surface: A newspaper boss fires the editor after scrutinising them for a brilliant replacement.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a brilliant celestial body, or a brilliant performer.

clue.text: Title we have secured by explosive series of games

indicators.note: secured by means held inside the explosive

parts.note: TNT is the explosive trinitrotoluene
what we have is ours, giving our
a title is a name

explanation.surface: Our championship title is guaranteed by a blistering run of matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosive series' reads as a single phrase, but 'explosive' gives TNT and 'series of games' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament is a competition made up of a sequence of matches.

clue.text: Knowing about key as something that might open windows?

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word goes round the letter

parts.note: knowing means aware
D is a musical key

explanation.surface: A knowledgeable person knows which key opens the windows.
explanation.walkthrough: The windows are pop-up windows on a computer screen, not house windows.
explanation.definitionFit: Adware is software that throws up advertising pop-ups on a computer screen.

clue.text: Ring to listen to one half of animated pair

indicators.note: to listen to means the answer is what you hear when the name is said
one half of means only the dog's name from the double act is the one heard

parts.note: the animated pair is Wallace and Gromit, the claymation inventor and his dog

explanation.surface: Someone phones to hear one of a famous cartoon double act.
explanation.walkthrough: Wallace and Gromit are the British plasticine claymation pair; 'Ring' looks like a phone call but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A grommet is a metal or rubber eyelet, a ring protecting a hole in material.

clue.text: Stop brewing herb tea with the last of water

indicators.note: brewing means stewing, so these letters are stirred into a new order
the last of picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Pausing to make herbal tea with the remaining water.
explanation.definitionFit: A breather is a short rest or pause from activity.

clue.text: Hooligan managed to get round two-thirds of gallery in Florence

indicators.note: to get round means the first word surrounds the second

parts.note: managed means ran, as in ran a business

indicators.note: two-thirds of means the final third of the word is dropped

parts.note: the Uffizi is the famous art gallery in Florence

explanation.surface: A thug in charge somehow tours most of a famous Italian gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Uffizi is Florence's great art gallery; 'two-thirds of' drops the last third of its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruffian is a violent, lawless person, much like a thug or lout.

clue.text: Terminally overweight friend

parts.note: overweight means fat
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A tactless jibe about a friend who is hopelessly overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatally means in a way causing death, as terminally ill does.

clue.text: Take husks off tough rice and such

definitions.text: Take husks off tough rice and such

indicators.note: the husks are the outer casings, so the outside letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: Instructions for preparing grain by stripping hard husks from rice and similar crops.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: threshing beats grain to separate it from its husk; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To thresh is to beat cereal crops such as rice so the grain separates from the chaff.

clue.text: Thwart special constable taking stimulant

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for special constable, a volunteer police officer in Britain
an upper is a stimulant drug

explanation.surface: A volunteer police officer is caught using drugs, wrecking the operation.
explanation.definitionFit: To scupper a plan is to sink or ruin it, so to frustrate it.

clue.text: What determines price of wagon on railway

indicators.note: on puts the wagon above the railway in this down entry

parts.note: a cart is a wagon
EL is an elevated railway, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: Pricing a goods wagon carried by rail.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartel is a group of producers that collude to fix prices.

clue.text: Stake a new note

parts.note: te is a note in the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A gambler stakes a fresh banknote.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the ante is the bet each player puts in before the deal.

clue.text: Brilliant singer at our carol broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A dazzling vocalist performs at a carol service that is aired on radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloratura is a soprano who sings elaborate, ornamented runs with dazzling agility.

clue.text: Boss is unintelligent, but not very religious

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so the letters are removed

parts.note: unintelligent means stupid
pi is short for pious, very religious

explanation.surface: A dim boss who is not especially devout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager, but is a stud: a raised ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a projecting knob or ornament, which is what a boss is.

clue.text: Into Hell he'd burst to maintain a position

indicators.note: burst means broken apart, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A soldier charged into hell to keep his ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold the line is the military idiom for refusing to give ground.

clue.text: Pawn the thing? That's mine

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn
the thing is it

explanation.surface: Someone claims a pawned object as their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like a possessive but is a coal mine; 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit is a coal mine, the shaft and workings dug to extract coal.

clue.text: Each day Iran backed capturing foreign capital

indicators.note: backed says the hidden letters are read backwards
capturing means holding inside, so the answer is held within these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Iran is said to support something every day.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft had 'capturing' in the definition; it is the hidden-word signal, so the definition is just 'foreign capital', and 'backed' turns the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: Riyadh is the capital city of Saudi Arabia, a country foreign to Britain.

clue.text: As hand waving left Tuaregs confused

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Bewildered Saharan nomads gesture as someone departs.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestural describes communication by gestures, like waving one's hands about.
